newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - June 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - June 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Morocco's economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Morocco will launch a tender on September 15 for building a port in the northern city of Tangier. Only five foreign groups -- American, French and Spanish-- have been invited to take part.

- Staff discontent grows in farmers' credit bank Caisse Nationale de Credit Agricole (CNCA) following two-day strike last week which brought no result. Workers' union threatens to hold sit-in if there are no talks by June 20.

- Morocco's early fruit and vegetable exports reached 254,170 tonnes in 1996-97 from 243,317 tonnes in 1995-96. Agriculture services company said the campaign had been "disastrous for tomatoes which faced additional fees on European markets.

- Morocco will soon start operating a private regional airline called Regional Air Lines which plans to service southern Agadir, Marrakesh and northern Tangier twice a day and later Tetuan in northern Morocco and Malaga in Spain during summer.
- Morocco is the biggest Arab insurance market and the second in Africa with receipts of seven billion dirhams ($738 million) in 1995 and nearly 30 billion dirhams of assets.
- British-Dutch ING-Barings brokers withdraw from Casablanca stock exchange in favour of Cairo bourse. It complains about expensive brokerage fees.
